Spec 02

How it works

How it works

UI DNA measures; your agent decides. Every step leaves evidence, and every value says where it came from.

02.1The loop

StepWhat happensWho decides
CaptureChromium loads each page at each viewport. UI DNA records the DOM, computed styles filtered to rendering properties, bounding boxes, the accessibility tree, form facts, fonts, assets, network metadata and one screenshot per state. It reads the page's stylesheet width conditions and resizes between the scanned widths to locate where the layout actually changes. With a crawl, same-origin links are followed breadth-first within a page budget; with body capture, JSON responses are stored as redacted data assets.UI DNA
ExploreHover, focus, Escape, Tab, and clicks on non-submitting buttons, summaries, tabs and disclosure or menu triggers, on every page. Search boxes of tables and lists are tried with a query taken from their items, then one that matches nothing, then cleared. Links to another crawled page are followed once and recorded as navigation transitions. The forms policy also fills each form with synthetic values and submits it empty and filled. Every non-GET request is blocked for the whole run. Every action is snapshotted, performed, diffed and reverted; every skip has a reason.UI DNA
MeasureTokens come from clustering measured values, with sample counts. Component candidates come from structural fingerprints across pages, with instances, varying props, variants and a confidence derived from agreement. Header and footer shared by every page become a layout. Repeated items become collections, and each transition that narrowed or reordered them is classified as a search, filter, sort or reset with the field that explains it.UI DNA
Understand and annotateThe agent reads the document, names components and tokens, records what it infers and why, and authorizes assets the user owns. Agent readings are stored as inferred next to the measured values, never over them.the agent
GenerateA deterministic React + TypeScript + Tailwind + Vite project: one component per page behind react-router, semantic HTML, extracted components, tokens as CSS variables and a Tailwind theme with the located breakpoints, observed transitions as React state with the original ARIA attributes, collections rendered through search, filter and sort state, forms with the observed validation messages, typed mocks from captured data, and a Playwright suite that replays the recorded transitions.UI DNA
VerifyPixel diff, SSIM, geometry, computed styles and element presence per page, state and viewport, plus the layout on both sides of every located breakpoint. Recorded transitions are replayed, including fills, blocked submits and navigations; after a search, filter or sort the generated items are compared with the original's by identity and order. The generated Playwright suite can run too. One finding per concrete difference, with the original and generated values.UI DNA
Repair and reportThe agent edits the project against the DiffReport and re-verifies; regressions and resolved findings are tracked per attempt. A static HTML report shows the evidence.the agent

Every value in the document carries provenance: measured, observed, inferred (agent only) or unknown with a reason. Nothing is rounded into a guess, and no result is a single blended score.

02.2What ships

Phase 1, the single-page loop. From URL to verified React project, proven in CI with a real Chromium against Fixture A, a marketing page with a responsive navbar and hamburger menu, a hero, two call-to-action buttons, a three-card grid, an image, an FAQ accordion and a footer, at 1280, 768 and 390 pixels wide.

  • Two browser modes: Playwright-launched Chromium for public pages, and attach to your own Chrome over the DevTools Protocol for sessions you are authorized to analyze.
  • robots.txt honored, per-origin rate limits, Chromium sandbox requested (with an honest limitation when the host cannot provide one), secrets redacted before anything is stored.
  • Twelve tools with one evidence envelope, identical over MCP and the CLI; setup and doctor on the CLI; --json, a config file and debug logging.
  • A versioned, framework-neutral schema published separately as uidna-schema.
  • The generated project builds; its build, the recorded transitions, and an injected CSS and behavior regression are each a CI test.

Phase 2, sites, forms, data, collections and breakpoints. Each capability below is a CI gate on its own fixture.

  • Multi-page crawl. crawl: { maxPages, include, exclude } follows same-origin links breadth-first; cross-origin links are recorded and never followed. Pages carry their depth and the link that discovered them. Components are matched across pages, and the header and footer every page shares become one layout.
  • Navigation transitions. A click on a link to another crawled page is recorded as a transition between the two pages. The generator wires it as a router link and the verifier replays it through the original link.
  • Forms. The forms policy fills controls with synthetic values (never real credentials; hidden and file inputs are never filled), submits the empty form to observe client-side validation and the filled form to observe the result. Validation states keep aria-invalid, the error message and the browser's validity. Every submission request is blocked, recorded as a side effect and never repeated.
  • Data. captureBodies: "json" stores JSON responses from fetch and XHR as redacted, size-capped data assets. The generator turns each one into a typed mock.
  • Responsive rules. Breakpoints are located where the layout actually changes, not at the scanned widths: stylesheet thresholds are read and confirmed one pixel apart by resizing, and changes no stylesheet explains are found by bisection within a budget. Probing only resizes the page and blocks every non-GET request. The document lists each breakpoint with its bracket and condition and the layout values that change there; the generator declares those breakpoints and attributes each style change to the one that explains it; the verifier checks the generated layout on both sides of each.
  • Search, filter and sort. Tables, lists and card grids become collections with item identity, fields and value kinds. A search box is tried with a query taken from the items' own text; chips, tabs and column headers are clicked as usual. Each change is classified against the base items: a search with its match and fields, a filter with the field and value it keeps, a sort with its field, direction and comparator, a reset. The generated project renders the items through that state, and the verifier compares the generated items with the original's by identity and order.
  • Row actions. A control repeated in every item of a collection (an "Archive" button per row) is one action: once it causes a side effect, it is skipped in every other item.
  • Behavior tests. The generated project includes tests/behavior.spec.ts: one Playwright test per implemented transition, asserting the observed delta. Transitions the generator did not reproduce, or that caused a side effect when observed, are skipped with the reason. verify_reconstruction runs the suite when asked.

Fixture B is an orders dashboard: a table loaded from a JSON endpoint with a search box, status chips and sortable columns, a row action that posts, and breakpoints at 600, 960 and 1100px, none of them a scanned width. Fixture C is a signup form with client-side validation, a POST endpoint and a JSON list. Fixture D is a three-page site with a shared header and footer, tabs, a pricing toggle and a cross-origin footer link.

02.3Authorized use

Scan interfaces you own or are allowed to analyze. UI DNA never bypasses authentication, CAPTCHAs, anti-bot measures or access controls, never stores credentials, and never redistributes third-party assets: unauthorized assets become labeled placeholders until you mark them authorized with annotate_dna. See DISCLAIMER.md and SECURITY.md.

Exploration blocks every non-GET request for the whole run, including beacons sent while a page unloads: an action that tries to send one is recorded as a side effect and never repeated, and the request never reaches its server. A page that loads its content with POST requests shows its error state instead. The forms policy types synthetic values into the page and runs its submit handlers; search boxes are typed into with text taken from the page's own items. Use them only on interfaces you may test that way. A crawl stays on the seed's origin, honors robots.txt and stops at its page budget.

To analyze an authenticated app, start your own Chrome with --remote-debugging-port=9222, open the page, then uidna scan --cdp-endpoint http://localhost:9222. The session stays yours; UI DNA reads the page and performs the same safe interactions.

02.4Limitations

  • A crawl follows same-origin <a href> links only, up to 50 pages. Navigations made by scripts are blocked and reported, not followed.
  • Server responses to form submissions are never observed, because the requests are blocked. Success states that depend on the server are reproduced only as far as the page showed them without one, and the generated README says so.
  • <iframe> content and shadow DOM are not entered; they are reported as limitations.
  • Inline <svg> markup is not captured; such nodes become placeholders.
  • Breakpoints are located from readable stylesheets and by resizing between the scanned widths. Cross-origin stylesheets, container queries and continuously varying values (clamp(), vw) are not breakpoints; a threshold above the widest or below the narrowest scanned width is read from the stylesheet but not seen. When two located breakpoints fall between the same scanned widths, a property that changes twice there is generated at the later one.
  • Collections are explored through search boxes outside forms, and through the chips, tabs and column headers the click round already clicks. Selects, checkboxes, combined filters, server-side search, pagination and load-more are not explored or reproduced; generated collections show the captured items, not the endpoint's data.
  • Spacing tokens are used values: a margin: auto shows up as the pixel margin it produced.
  • Hover and focus transitions are reproduced as CSS variants at every viewport. Click toggles are reproduced, sharing their state across section files when the changed nodes live elsewhere; component instances changed together with nodes outside them are rendered inline instead. Every behavior the generator could not implement is listed in the generated README and skipped in its Playwright suite.
  • The generator is a baseline, not a finished product: names are placeholders and the agent is expected to repair against the DiffReport.
  • Verification compares at the scanned viewports with system fonts; cross-machine pixel diffs reflect font rendering differences, which is why findings carry the measured values rather than a single score.
